This is an unverified tesseract dump of all 552 leaves of the Gale scan of

    Wm. M. Caswell, comp., Revised Charter and Compiled Ordinances and
    Resolutions of the City of Los Angeles (Evening Express Steam Printing
    Establishment, 1878).  Gale, The Making of Modern Law: Primary Sources,
    doc id DT0106137878.

It exists so the volume can be GREPPED. It is NOT a transcription and nothing
in it has been checked by eye.

*** WHAT IT IS FOR:  finding out which page a word is on.
*** WHAT IT IS NOT FOR:  quoting, citing, or reading a section number off.

The verified text -- both indexes line by line, and the full text of every
renaming instrument -- is in  caswell-1878-contents.md  beside this file.
Anything destined for an excerpt or a row must come from there, or from a
fresh read of the page image.

KNOWN FAILURE MODES OF THIS DUMP, all observed while checking it:
  * SECTION NUMBERS ARE UNRELIABLE.  They are printed small in the outer
    margin and tesseract routinely reads 3 as 9 and 5 as 6: real section 361
    came out "861", 244 came out "944", 245 as "945", 702 as "709".
  * PAGE NUMBERS IN THE INDEX ARE UNRELIABLE.  Leader dots run into the
    figures: real "582 352" came out "682 852"; real "274 152" came out
    "274 182".
  * Dark versos and blank leaves produce pages of pure noise.
  * Long s, ligatures, 1/2 and 3/4 fractions, degree signs and the Spanish
    names (Sepulveda, Sansevaine, Marchessault, Olivas) are all shaky.

ARTICLE XII.
MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS.
SECTION 1. The city of Los Angeles shall not be, and is

Contracts. not, bound by any contract, or in any way liable thereon,
unless the same is made in writing by order of the Council,
the draft thereof be approved by the Council, and the same
Ordered to be, and be, signed by the Mayor, or some other
person, in behalf of the city; but the Mayor and Council, by
an ordinance, or the Council, by a resolution or motion, may
authorize any officer, committee or agent of the city, to
bind the city, without a contract in writing, for the payment
of any sum of money not exceeding three hundred dollars;
provided, that no contract binding the city shall be valid
unless it be completely executed, fulfilled and performed
within the period of two years after the date of the execu-
tion and delivery thereof. %

Corporation Src. 2. The said corporation shall not be liable to any

oe for one, or for any loss or injury to person or property growing
out of, or caused by, the malfeasance, misfeasance, or neglect
of duty of any officer, or other authorities of said city; or
for any injury or damages happening to such person or prop-
erty on account of the condition of any zanja, sewer, cess-
pool, street, sidewalk or public ground therein; but this does
not exonerate any officer of said city, or any other person,
from such liability, when such causality or accidentis caused
hy the willful neglect of duty enforced upon such officer or
person by law, or by the gross negligence or willful miscon-
duct of such officer or person in any other respect.

the bank thus selected, all public moneys of said city by him
collected or received. For each such deposit the Treasurer
shall take the receipt of the bank, and from and after the
deposit of sueh money in said bank the Treasurer and his
bondsmen shall no longer be liable therefor. Should the City Treasur-
City Treasurer refuse or neglect at any time to comply with f2; Penalty
the orders of the Council, as to the deposit of such moneys,

shall retain the possession or control ef such moneys; or he

this State, applicable thereto, to compel such deposits to be
made.

RULES OF THE CITY COUNCIL.
a ee
The following rules shall be observed in conducting the
business of the City Council, viz.:
(See McPherson’s compilations, page 28.)
RULE I.

The President shall take the chair at the hour appointed
for the Council to meet, and shall immediately call the mem-
bers to order.

RULE II.

At the stated meetings of the Council, the reading of the
journal of the preceding, stated and intervening special meet-
ings, shall first be in order, unless unanimously dispensed
with, and the unfinished business appearing thereon shall be
then disposed of, unless otherwise directed by the Council.

| RULE III.

After a motion is stated by the Chairman or read by the
Clerk, it may be withdrawn by the mover at any time before
decision or amendment.

RULE IV. :

When demanded by any member present, the ayes and
noes shall be entered on the journal, and they shall be taken
upon the passage of every ordinance and entered on the
journal.

RULE V.

No member shall vote when personally interested in the
decision of the question before the Council, nor shall any
member be security on any bond, note or obligation given to
the city.

===== PDF 58  [printed p. 58] =====

o8 REVISED CHARTER.
RULE VI.

The Standing Committees shall be as follows:

Board of Public Works.

Committee on Finance,

a ‘© Police.

J ‘t Sewers.

6 ‘¢ Fire and water.
- ‘© Zanjas.

a se Land.

ts ‘© Parks.

cs ct Gas.

sd ‘¢ Supplies.

Board of Health.

And the Mayor shall be ex-officio a member of all stand-
ing committees.

: RULE VII. \

After calling the roll and reading minutes of the pre-
vious meeting, the order of business shall be as follows:

1. Communications from the Mayor.

2. Reports of Committees.

3. Reports of Officers.

4, Petitiens, Memorials and Communications.

5. Claims against the city.

6. Miscellaneous matters.

RULE VIII.
Every member, previous to speaking, shall address him-
self to the President.
RULE IX.
When two or more members speak at the same time, the
President shall decide who is entitled to the first hearing.
RULE X.

When the President desires to leave the chair, he shall
appoint some member of the Council to fill the same, pro tem.
RULE XI.

When an amendment to a resolution is moved and sec-
onded, the vote shall, in all cases, be first upon the amend-
ment, unless the mover of the resolution shall accept such
amendment.

===== PDF 59  [printed p. 59] =====

REVISED CHARTER. 59
RULE XII.

A motion to refer to a committee, or lay on the table,
shall, if seconded, preclude all amendments to the main
question until such motion is decided.

RULE XII.

The previous question being moved and seconded, shall

preclude all further debate until it has been decided.
RULE XIV.

A vote of two-thirds of all the members present shall

be necessary to suspend the rules.
RULE XV..

When a question has been once put and decided, it shall
be in order for any member who voted in the majority to
move for the reconsideration thereof; but no motion for the
reconsideration of any vote shall be made after the ordi-
nance or resolution, shall have gone out of the possession of
the Board ; and no motion of reconsideration shall be made
more than once.

RULE XVI.
__ No person shall speak more than twice to the same ques-
tion without leave of the Board; nor more than once until
every member choosing to speak shall have spoken; nor
more than onee upon the previous question.

RULE XVII.

When a motion is seconded, it shall be stated by the
President before debate ; and every such motion shall be re-
duced to writing, if any member desire it.

RULE XVIII.

After a motion is stated’ by the President, it shall be
deemed to bein possession of the Board ; but it may be with-
drawn at any time before decision or amendment.

RULE XIX.

When the question is under debate, no motion shall be
received, unless

1. To amend it.

2. To commit it.

8. To lay on the table.

4. To postpone,

5. The previous question,

6. To adjourn.

===== PDF 60  [printed p. 60] =====

60 REVISED CHARTER.
RULE XxX.

A motion to adjourn shall always be in order, and shall
be decided without debate.

RULE XXI.

Every member who shall be present when a question is
put, shall vote for or against the same unless the Board shall
excuse him, or unless he be immediately interested in the
question, in which case he shall not vote; buf no member
shall be permitted to vote upon a question when a division is
called, unless present when his name is called in its regular
order.

RULE XXII.

A member called to order shall immediately sit down,
unless permitted to explain; and the Board, if appealed to,
shall decide on the case, but without debate. If there be no
appeal, the decision of the Chair shall be submitted to.

RULE XXIII.

Any member may call fora division, and the names of
those who vote for and those who vote against a question,
shall be entered upon the minutes ; and in all cases required
by law, and in all appropriations of public money, the ayes
and noes shall be called by the Clerk, and recorded.

RULE XXIV.

In all divisions taken by the Board, on the call of a mem-
ber, it shall be the duty of the Clerk to enter on the minutes
the names of the members so calling for a division.

. RULE XXV.

A committee appointed to report on any subject shall
report the facts in relation to the matter or subject referred,
with their opinions thereon in writing ; and no report shall
be received as the report of a committee, except the same be
signed by a majority of the committee; but nothing herein
contained shall prevent a minority from submitting their
report, which may be read, if called for.

RULE XXVI.

All claims against the city shall be first presented to the
Finance Committee, who shall audit and examine the same,
and, if found correct, shall endorse thereon the fact.

===== PDF 61  [printed p. 61] =====

REVISED CHARTER. 61
RULE XXVII.

No member shall absent himself without permission

from the President. .
RULE XXVIII.

The President, in all cases, has the right ef voting; and
wher the Board shall be equally divided, including his vote,
the question shall be lost.

RULE XXIX.

Whenever it shall be moved and earried that the Board
go into a committee of the whole, the President shall leave
the chair, and shall appoint a chairman of the committee of
the whole, who shall report the proceedings of the committee.

Ordinances and Resolutions

ALIENATION OF CITY LANDS.

AN ORDINANCE concerning the municipai lands.

The Common Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain
as follows: '

1 SECTION 1. All the vacant lands belonging to the city
of Los Angeles, except those hereafter enumerated, may be
disposed of in conformity with this ordinance.

Sec. 2. Any person who may desire to procure lands
belonging to the city, for the purpose of cultivation, shall
present his petition to the Mayor of the city, setting forth
accurately the description, by metes and bounds, as near as
may be, and the length and breadth, by yards, of the lot of
land applied for, together with the names of the owners or
possessors of land in the immediate neighborhood.

Sec. 3. Upon the receipt of the petition, the Mayor
shall cause the Marshal to notify the owners or possessors of
lands in the neighborhood, of the presentation of the peti-
tion, who shall be entitled to appear and contest the applica-
tion, upon a day to be fixed by the Mayor, which shall not °
be less than one week after filing the petition. ,

Src. 4. Upon the day fixed, the Mayor, if he find that
there are no conflicting claims, and that it is otherwise fit
and proper, may grant a certificate of possession to the peti-
tioner, which shall have reference to this ordinance, where-
by he shall be entitled to enter and possess the said tract of
land for the term of one year from the date of his certificate,

Src. 5. In no ease shall a lot of more than ten acres,
within the limits of the city, or thirty-five acres without
said limits, be granted as aforesaid by the Mayor.

Src. 6. Upon the presentation of any petition, as afore-
said, the petitioner shall pay to the Mayor ten: dollars, to
pay the expenses incurred by his application ; of said sum

===== PDF 66  [printed p. 66] =====

66 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

the Marshal shall receive two dollars whenever there is a

notification to the neighboring owners or possessors; the

Mayor shall receive four dollars, in full for his services
and the balance shall be deposited in the city treasury, to

the credit of the land fund, and shall be used as the Common

Council shall hereafter determine,

Src. 7. No person shall be entitled to receive more than
two certificates of possession under the provisions of this
ordinance; nor shall the number of acres granted to any
person by the said one or two certificates, ever exceed the
quantity prescribed in Section five, to-wit: in all, thirty-five
acres.

Src. 8. The Mayor shall keep, in a well bound book, a
record of all his proceedings under this ordinance, and shall
file all the petitions for lands in his office; and, at every meet-
ing of the Common Council, on or subsequent to the first day
of each month, shall transmit a report of all the certificates
of possession which he may have issued, which shall be con-
sidered approved, unless the Common Council, by resolution,
within one month after his said report, annul or disallow
them; in which case they shall be considered of no effect.

Sec. 9. Immediately after the qualification of the new
members of the Common Council elected ata general munic-
ipal election, they shall name, by ballot thereof, their mem-
bers as a board of adjudication of municipal lands, who
shall have power, upon the petition of the grantees of the
certificates of posession, to hear, at the expiration of one
year from the date of their granting by the Mayor, their ap-
plication to have a title in fee simple made out to them by
the city.

Sec. 10. If, upon the hearing of said petition, the board
be satisfied that the said petitioner, in good faith, has im-
proved the tract or tracts of municipal lands described in his
certificate of possession, by building, planting orange or
other fruit trees, or cultivating crops thereon; provided,
however, that said improvements shall never be less than
two hundred dollars, they shall certify said facts to the
Mayor, Who is hereby authorized to execute and acknowl-
edge a deed of the land described in his certificate or cer-
tificates of possession to the petitioner, in the name or on
the bebalf of the city; which said deed shall Specially re-
fer to this ordinance and be subject to the conditions herein
contained.

Sec. 11. But if the said board shall be satisfied that

_ the said improvements have not been made in good faith,

===== PDF 67  [printed p. 67] =====

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 67
they shall also certify this fact to the Mayor, who shall
be authorized to issue a certificate of possession to any
party applying therefor, for the land described in the cer-
tificate of the petitioner to said board.

Sec. 12. If any person, within one year from the date
of his certificate, shall fail to make the proofs as set forth
in Section ten (10), the Mayor may grant possession of
said land to any person applying, as of vacant city land;
provided, nevertheless, that if the original holder of the
first certificate be in possession, he shall, on petition, be
entitled to a preference.

Sec. 13. The conditions upon which all of said grants
and deeds shall be made are: that upon said lands the city
shall always have the right to establish public roads and
cross-roads sufficient for four-wheeled carriages, and 1n what-
ever direction may be necessary ; with aqueducts and canals
of water for common use; common sewers and private irri-
gation; and all owners shall facilitate the entrance into
said lands to the officers encharged with the conservation,
distribution and arrangement of the water, and to the
laborers engaged in the cleaning and conservation of the
aqueducts; nor prohibiting the neighbors from entering to
direct and facilitate the passage of the waters to their fields
or gardens (cuando les), when it corresponds to them by ;
ordinances; and the favored persons, at all times, although
they may be out of the limits of the jurisdiction of the city,
shall pay whatever tax that is, or may be, established for
the use of the water, the same as that paid by residents and
owners within said limits; and shall be subject, and will con-
form, to whatever general system of water that may be es-
tablished by competent authority. A violation of these con-
ditions will cause to the owner a forfeiture of his right to
the land granted or confirmed by title, and the land shall
be subject to confiscation for the benefit of the city of Los
Angeles.

Sxc. 14. After having practiced all due diligence, as pre-
scribed in this ordinance, to see if the land is public, unoc-

_ cupied land, if there is no obstacle to the adjudication, it
shall be made ; measuring the land; observing between him-
self and others the corresponding boundaries; demarking
there upon the ground the spaces that are to remain for
streets or passage ways; assisting in the operation one or

more individuals of the commission. ;
Src. 15. All improved lands; all lands blocked or lined

===== PDF 68  [printed p. 68] =====

68 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

off on the city plan; the hill called Fort Hill; the hill in
rear of the houses of Pio Pico, are hereby exempted from the
provisions of this ordinance.

SrEc. 16. The lands comprehended in the certificates, and
which are the objects of this ordinance, cannot be sold,
pledged, nor in any manner alienated, only by the permis-
sion of the Common Council, except when the owner shall
have perfected his title.

SEc. 17. Those whose lands shall approach within fifty
yards of the edge of the river shall have the liberty of occu-
pying up to the river’s bank, which adjudication shall be
made in conformity with this ordinance; and no certificate
shall be given for land facing on the river, for more than

. four hundred yards.

Sec. 18. All lands embraced in the certificates of pos-
session, issued under this ordinance, shall bein formas nearly
square as possible.

Sec. 19. That the Mayor be empowered to grant, on ap-
plication, all building lots belonging to the city subject to
the provisions heretofore set forth in this ordinance, except-
ing squares already reserved for public use,

Src. 20. This ordinance shall take effect from the date
of its publication.

MANUEL REQUENA,
President of the Common Council.
Approved August 13th, 1852.
JOHN G. NICHOLS, Mayor.
WM. G. DRYDEN, Secretary.

AN ORDINANCE to repeal an ordinance concerning municipal

lands, approved August 13th, 1852.

The Mayor, Recerder and Common Council of the city of Los

Angeles do ordain as follows:

SECTION 1. The ordinance entitled an ordinance con-
eerning municipal lands, approved August 13th, 1852, is.
hereby repealed.

SEc. 2. The lands and lots, the complete title to which 9
is yet pending, shall, at the proper time, be adjudged to the
persons to whom they have been granted, if they comply
with the provisions of said ordinance; otherwise the said
lands and lots shall revert to the city.

===== PDF 69  [printed p. 69] =====

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 69

Src. 3. This ordinance shall take effect from the day of
its publication.

Passed May 19th, 1854.

AN ORDINANCE to determine the front line of the houses of .
this city, which are separated from the streets in the de-
lineation and formation of the plan of this city.

The Mayor, Recorder and Common Council of the city of Los
Angeles do ordain as follows: .

3 Src. 1. The houses whose fronts are separated from the
streets of the city since the plan of the city has been formed,
ean establish their fronts on the line of the nearest street, at
the choice of the owner, and the city relinquishes in favor of
the owners of such houses all the right # may have to the
land between the house and the street.

Src. 2. This ordinance shall take effect from the date of
its publication, and repeals the municipal decree of March
23d, 1854.

FRANCIS MELLUS, President.

STEPHEN C. FOSTER, Mayor.

Approved May 20, 1854.

(See Records Los Angeles City, Vol. II, p. 26.)

(The following ordinance is copied from Article seven, of the
revised ordinances, adopted July 31st, 1855, and is be-
lieved to be the same in effect of an ordinance ap-
proved by the Council June, 30th, 1854, the original
of which is missing. A rough draft of a similar ordi-
nance is found in Vol. VII, of the Archives, but not ap-
proved):

OF THE ALIENATION OF CITY LANDS.

4 Sroctron 1. All personsthat wish to obtain from the city
of Los Angeles, lots, or fractions of lots, or lands, shall de-
posit in the office of the Mayor a descriptive notice of the
lot, or fraction of a lot or lands they desire, setting forth the
location, boundary and dimensions exactly as may be shown
on the city map, and survey of adjacent lands.

Src. 2. Upon the third Wednesday of each month, after
notice of sale has been given for two weeks prior thereto,
said notice to be given by the Mayor, by causing the same to
be posted upin writing in three conspicuous places in the

===== PDF 70  [printed p. 70] =====

70 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS
city, one of which shall be the door of the Mayor’s office, and
in the discretion of the Mayor, one publication of the same
in some publie newspaper printed in the city, the Mayor
shall offer at publie auction, in frout of the door of his office,
for cash in band, between the hours of ten and twelve of
the forenoon, the lots or fractions of lots or lands that
shall have been solicited during the previous month, selling
the same to the highest bidder; provided, that the mini-
mum bid that shall be received for any tract of land known
as thirty-five acre lots, and fraetions of the same lying con-
tiguous thereto, shall be one dollar per acre; and for any
other lot containing more than ten and not exceeding
thirty-four, the minimum bid to be received shall be two
dollars per acre; and for any lot containing more than one
acre, and not exceeding ten acres, the minimum bid to be
received shall be four dollars per acre; and for any lot less
than one acre, the minimum bid to be received shall be
twenty dollars; and for any fraction of a lot, less than one
acre, contiguous to any lot except a thirty-five acre tract,
the minimum bid to be received shall be twenty dollars;
and provided further, that the hours of sale designated in
this section may be extended until four o’clock, P. M. of
the same day, at the discretion of the Mayor.

Src. 38. The Mayor shall receive the purchase meney,
and give the purchaser a quit claim deed, and shall note the
same in the book of record wherein are preserved concessions
of municipal lands since the 13th of August, A. D. 1852.
And for each lot, or fraction of a lot or tract quit claimed by
him in obedience to this ordinance, he shall receive five
dollars, whieh shall be deducted from the amount of sales,
and shall pay the remainder into the city treasury ; provided,
that if any purchaser of more than one lot or tract of land
shall require the same put into one deed, the said purchaser
shall pay the extra fee of the Mayor jor each lot exceed-
ing one.

Sc. 4. All lands improved or disposed of in accordance
with previous ordinances and resolutions which are hereby
ratified; aud the lots Nos. 3 and 8 of each parallelogram upon
the cjty map, which were not previously disposed of before
the ordinance of July 7, 1854, Fort Hill, and the round hillin
the rear of the house of Pio Pico, occupied as the Land Office _
of the United States, and all the lands that have useful stone
for building or lime, are all exceptions to the provisions of
this ordinance, as all lands that have not been regularly sur-
veyed by order of the Common Council, and platted, which

===== PDF 71  [printed p. 71] =====

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 71
plat or plats shall be on file in the Mayor’s office, except frac-
tions of lots within the fire limits of the city, contiguous to
lots already surveyed ; provided, that nothing in this ordi-
nance shall prevent the Common Council from disposing of
the public domain from time to time as may be thought
necessary to meet the demands of public and private utility.
AN ORDINANCE amendatory of ‘An Ordinance Providing

for the Alienation of City Lands.”

Be it ordained by the Mayor and Common Council of the

City of Los Angeles, as follows:

5 SECTION 1. That an ordinance, providing for the alien-
ation of city lands, approved July 31st, A. D. 1855, be, and
the same is hereby amended, by adding Section 5thin the
words, as follows:

That all and every fractional lot of land on either side of
the Los Angeles river, and facing thereon, are hereby re-
served for public use, and the same shall not be sold to
private individuals; provided, however, that by special
ordinance the city may dispose of said lands.

A. F. CORONEL,
President of the Common Council.
Approved October 12th, 1857.
JOHN G. NICHOLS, Mayor.
W.G. DRYDEN, Clerk.

there shall be appropriated two thousand five hundred dol-

Sec. 2, This expenditure shall be made now, advancing

same shall be concluded and delivered to the city, the part of
the jail which will belong to the city, by a resolution and
decree of the Board of Supervisors, the remaining one
thousand dollars shall be paid.

SEC. 3. Repealed.

- AN ORDINANCE requiring the boundary lines of lands con-

ceded by the city to be distinctly marked.

10 SECTION 1. Theindividuals who may have received a

donation of land from the city, and those who in future may

receivea grant of land, in conformity with the ordinance of

the 13th of August, 1352, shall place their corners and linesin

such a manner as to be permanent and make Known their

respective boundaries; and this city will not be responsible by

indemnification of any kind, which may originate by an
infraetion of this ordinance.

Approved July 7, 1853.

MANUEL REQUENA, President.

Dolores Abila.

It shall be the duty of the Marshal and policemen to
take up and impound any of said animals found at large
upon the streets within said limits, and for each animal so

imal; provided, that they shall not receive more than ten

If there be no demand for any of the animals thus im- 86
pounded, or if the claimant refuse to pay the rate of fees and
charges allowed for impounding said animals, the Pound
Keeper is authorized and directed to advertise the same for
sale by posting up three written or printed notices in English
and Spanish, one of which shall be placed on the entrance of
the city pound, one on the bulletin board of the Mayor’s
office, the other on the Court House, giving the description,
with the marks and brands of said animal, for five days; and
for each animal so advertised the Pound Keeper shall be
entitled to twenty-five cents, to be collected as hereinafter
provided ; and on the day advertised shall offer for sale, to
the highest bidder, for each said animal or animals, provided
the bid is sufficient, or more than enough to cover the ex-

penses incurred in impounding and advertising said animals,
and after deducting his fees for the whole number of days

said animals were impounded, and for costs of advertising,
and the fee of the officer who may have impounded them,
shall pay the remainder, if any, at once to the City Treasur-
er for the use of the owner if claimed within six months
thereafter; if not, the same shall be applied to the use of the
City Hospital. Amended May 17th, 1877.

APPLICATION FOR TITLE IN CERTAIN CASES.

Any person or persons occupying or possessing lands be- 110
longing to the City of Los Angeles, and desirous of obtaining
a title to the same from the city, shall file a petition there-
for, together with a map and description of the land prayed
for, with the Clerk of the Common Council, at least six days
before the regular session day of the said Common Council.

Immediately on the filing of such petitions with the 111
Clerk of the Common Council, the Clerk of said Com-
mon Council shall cause to be published in some newspaper
published in the City of Los Angeles, a notice, for at least
five days, consecutively, before the regular meeting of said
Common Council, to the effect that the petition, or petitions
have been filed with him, praying for titles to the lands
described therein, and that the same will be had at the reg-
ular session of the Common Council. Said notice, in all
cases, to contain a description of the land prayed for, and
the name of the petitioner, together with a notice to all par-
ties interested therein to file their objections, if any they
have, in writing, with the Clerk of the Common Council, at
least one day before the regular session of that body, next

after the first publication of such notice or notices.

Any person or persons obtaining title or deeds to any 112
lands, under the provisions of this ordinance, shail, in ad-
dition to the necessary costs of executing the deeds therefor,
by the Mayor, pay the costs of such publication; nor shall
any deed be executed by the Mayor, and delivered to the per-
gon or persons to whom the same has been awarded by the
Common Gouncil, until the costs of such publication shall
be paid.

Nothing in this ordinanee shall be so construed as to ap- 113
ply in any manner to the sale of lands by the city at public
auction, or to affect the ordinances governing the same.

Any person applying for lands, and filing their petition
for the same with the Clerk of the Common Council, shall

of the proceeds of any such sale must be returned to the
owner of the property sold, and until claimed, must be de-
posited in the city treasury, subject to the owner, heirs or
legal representatives, if demanded within one year; and if
not called for before that time by the person entitled thereto,
the same shali be transferred to the Current Expense Fund;
provided, the same shall be refunded to the parties entitled
thereto, upon demand, without interest.

168 The City Tax Collector must annually, on the first Mon-

AN ORDINANCE granting certain privileges in the city of

Los Angeles to the Southern Pacific Railroad Company.
The Mayor and Common Council of the City of Los Angeles

do ordaiu as follows:

183 SECTION 1. That theright of way for the railroad track
of the Southern Pacific Railroad Company in and out of the
city of Los Angeles, for the distance said Company may
wish to use the same, be, and the same is hereby granted to
said Company, its successorsand assigns, over and upon the
street and its extension, commonly called Alameda street.
The said Company to locate its track or tracks as near the :
center of the street as may be; and the residue of said street
to be held and used by said city for the passage of persons and
vehicles on each side of the same; provided, that said city
expressly reservesthe right to locate cross streets over and

‘ across any part of Alameda street and railroad track, as the
future improvements and convenience of the city may re-
quire; and the Railroad Company, in consideration of said
right of way, agree to provide and keep in repair convenient
crossings over their track or tracks at the erossing of such
streets now in use, or which may be hereafter located by said
city. And, provided further, that said city reserves the right
to construct and pass under said railroad track any water
canal or zanja, or water ditch, at the expense of said city, its
successors or assigns, which may become necessary for the
use of the inhabitants of said city. The said railroad com-
pany, its successors and assigns, to correspond the track of
said road to the required grade of water canals, zanjas or
ditches now in use; and, provided further, that said railroad
track or tracks shall correspond to the official grade of said
street.

SEc. 2 Said Company are authorized to build ever or

- under any of the city zanjas; provided, that the same are
put in a safe and secure Operating condition at such crosa-
ings, by and at the expense of the company, wherever such
crossing interfere with the existing channels.

Seo. 3. For purposes of information to be acquired, the
said company are hereby empowered to enter upon any
street, lane or alley, or other city property, for purposes of
survey and with engineering parties, and to examine and
survey any waters within the control of the city. Approved
September 6th, 1872.

A map and plan of the bed of Los Angeles river, as sur- 184
veyed by A. F. Waldemar in Ihe month of November, A. D.
1862, is hereby declared to be official, and the courses and
boundaries prescribed in said map for said river are declared
to be the official city boundaries of said river.

All lands belonging to the city of Los Angeles and ac-
quired by the change in the bed of Los Angeles river, as pre- 189

: scribed by the plan of the bed of the Los Angeles river by
a survey of January 5th, 1863, and approved by the Mayor on
the same day and declared official, is hereby given to the
owners of land upon the borders of said river, so as to run to
the official established bed of said river, within the following
limits, and under the following conditions, to-wit: Com-
mencing at the city water-wheel and on the western side of
said river, extending down the whole length of the river
within the city limits; and on the eastern side, commencing
at the main point and extending down to the land known as
the land of Martin Lelong; the conditions upon which said
lands are granted, are: that the owners of said lands, border-
ing on said river, shall put eut a live fence on their lines to
the river bed, as declared in said official map; and the said
live fence is to extend along up and down the banks of the
said established river bed, along its eastern or western banks,
as the case may be; and, provided further, that said lines of
live fence be built within the period of eighteen months.

Maps No. 2, No. 3 and No. 4 are declared to be official
maps of the city of Los Angeles; and the President of the 186

FIRE DEPARTMENT.

There is hereby created a Fire Department, in and for the ]95
city of Los Angeles, to consist of not mere than three steam
fire engine eompanies, to consist each of a President, Vice-
President, Secretary and Treasurer, Foreman and First and
Second Assistant Foreman; also, one Engineer, one Driver,
one Fireman and eight Hosemen, and eight Axemen; also,

a Standing Committee of fiye members.

Two Hook and Ladder Companies, to consist each of one
Foreman, one Driver, one Tillerman and twelve Hook and
Laddermen, one of whom shall act as Assistant Foreman and
one as Clerk.

Three Hose Companies, to consist each of one Foreman,
one Driver, one Stewart and six Hosemen, one of whom shall
act as Assistant-Foreman and one as Clerk.

Each Fire Engine Company shall have one steam fire
engine, one hose reel, one thousand feet of hose, and not more
than three horses, .

Each Hook and Ladder Company shall have one truck
with hooks and ladders, and necessary and proper appurte-
nances and appliances, and not more than three horses.

Each Hose Company shall have one cart and reel, with
one thousand feet of hose; but the Common Council shall
have power to increase the number of Fire Companies as
the public safety of the city may require, and to purchase the
necessary steam engines, apparatus and appurtenances there-
for.

The only engines thatshall be purchased by the city and 196
used by the Fire Department, shall be steam fire engines of .
the best pattern and manufacture.

A Steam Fire Engine Company shall be composed of not 197

===== PDF 123  [printed p. 123] =====

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 123
more than sixty-five nor less then twenty-five males, of full
age—of twenty-one years; all of whom must be duly regis-
tered members of the Department. A company desiring ad-
mission intothe Department must make application to the
Common Couneil of the City of Los Angeles, accompanying
such application with a copy of their constitution, signed by
at least twenty-five males, of the age of twenty-one years,
the names of their officers, and where they desire to be lo-
cated. If such application receives the approval of the Com-
mon Council, the company shall be declared admitted into
the Department, and entitled to the privileges of the same.

198 Whenever aFire Company, by reason of death’s visita-
tions or expulsions shall have reduced its roll to less than
twenty-five active members, it shall be the duty of the Clerk
or Secretary of said Company to forthwith notify the Com-
mon Council of the fact, and such company shall thereupon
be forthwith suspended until the next regular meeting of
said Common Council, und if not increased to at least twen-
ty-five active members, by new membership before such next
regular meeting, and the names of such new members, to-
gether with the names of the active members remaining, re-
ported to said Common Council, it shall thereupon be dis-
banded.

ESTABLISHING RATES OF HACK HIRE AND DE-
.FINING THE DUTIES OF HACK DRIVERS IN
THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES.

900 It shall not be lawful for any hackman, coach or car-_
riage driver, for hire, to charge any higher rates than the
rates hereinafter in this ordinance prescribed; and for every
violation of this ordinance by any owner or driver of any
such hack, coach or carriage, the person so offending, on con-
viction thereof, shall be fined in any sum not less than five
dollars, and not exceeding twenty-five dollars, and costs of
the action.

901 For all service each hackman, coach or earriage driver
shall be allowed to charge for the use of the same, within the
limits, the following rates, to-wit. For the use of hacks for
the first hour, $2.50; for each subsequent hour, $1.50; from the

===== PDF 124  [printed p. 124] =====

124 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS
city hotels to the railroad depot, and from the depot to the
hotels, $1; where there is more than one person, then for each
one, 50 cents; for funerals, $5; for christenings, $2.50; for the
use of hack for one mile, $1; when more than one person,
then 50 cents for each one; and for all detention of hack, then
for such detention the same price as above by the hour,
It shall be the duty of each owner or driver of every 909
hack, eoach or earriage, to procure of the Clerk of the City
: Council the respective number for each hack, coach or
carriage, and place the same in some conspicuous place on
such hack, coach or carriage. It shall also be the duty of
such owner or driver to have lamps lighted on their vehicles,
always at night, while engaged in conveying passengers
through the streets of the city; also, to have printed rates of
fare posted in some conspicuous place inside of eaeb vehicle.
No hackman, coach, carriage or omnibus driver shall be 903
permitted to drive at an immoderate gait or dangerous speed
within the streets of said city, nor in any case permit their
horses to gallop or run; nor in any case to race in said streets
of the city; nor shall any person be permitted to drive any
sueh carriages, hacks, omnibuses or coaches, under the age
of eighteen years; and each hackman shall wear a badge,
designating the number of his hack, in a conspicuous place.
Amended July 17th, 1873; February 25th, 1875; July Sth, 1875;
August 12th, 1875; May 238d, 1878.
It is hereby declared unlawful for any person or persons 904
te leave unfastened and unattended to, any horse, either at-
tached to any vehicle or not, on the public streets of Los An-
geles; buf it shall be the duty of all persons to safely secure
their horses, and if found unhitched, it shall be the duty of
the police officers of the city to secure said animals and to
arrest the owners thereof ; and any person violating the pro-
visions of this section shall be liable to a fine of not less
than five dollars, nor more than twenty-five dollars, on con-
viction thereof before any Court of competent jurisdiction.
Approved May 24th, 1872.

SALE OF CITY LANDS.

An ordinance of date August 13th, 1852, donating certain 940
lands of the city on certain conditions is repealed; and from
and after this date (February 5th, 1866,) no deed shall be given
for any city land claimed under said ordinance.

All and every fractional lot of land on either side of the 94]
Los Angeles river and facing thereon are hereby reserved for
public use, and the same shall not be sold to private indi-
viduals; provided, however, that by special ordinance the
city may dispose of said lands.

The Mayor shall receive the purchase money, and give 949,
the purchaser a quit-claim deed, and shall note the same in
the book of record wherein are preserved concessions of mu-
nicipal lands since the 13th day of August, 1852. And for
each lot or fraction of a lot or tract quit-claimed by him in
obedience to this ordinance, he shall receive five dollars,
which shall be deducted from the amount of sales, and shal)
pay the remainder into the city treasury.

Money received for the sales of all city lands shall be paid 9.43
into the cash fund. Approved June Ist, 1869.

CHAIN GANG.

987 That hereafter all persons who shall be sentenced to work
upon the streets, or other public works in the city of Los An-
geles, by the Mayor’s Court, or by the County Court of Los
Angeles county, or by any of the Justices’ of the Peace
Courts in Los Angeles township, shall be delivered to the
City Marshal, or to such other police officer of the city or
other officer or person as the City Council may appoint, by
the Sheriff, Constable or Jailor, who may have them in cus-
tody, upon request of such city authorities.

988 The overseer of said chain-gang shall have full power to

F govern, control and direct all such persons while under his
control and in his custody, to compel them to perform labor
upon the streets or any other public works of the city; and
to this end may enforce all needful rules aad regulations
which may now be exercised and enforced over the convicts
in the State Prison, in order to enforce obedience and compel
the performance of labor and good discipline.

989 If any such prisoner shall, during his term of sentence,
escape, or attempt to escape, he shall be guilty of a misde-

. meanor and violation of this ordinance, and upon arrest and

5 conviction shal! be fined not exceeding one hundred dollars,
and may be sentenced to labor in double the time of his first
sentence to labor, with the costs of the aetion.

990 If any officer or person, having any of said chain-gang
in his charge, shall wilfully permit any one, or more, to es-
cape, he shall, forevery such offence, on conviction thereof,
be fined in not less than the fine of such offenders so permit-
ted to escape, with costs of the action, before any Court of
competent jurisdiction.

99] Persons sentenced to perform such labor may discharge
themselves at any time on payment of the amount which
may be due of the fine and costs, if any such shall be due.

The prisoners shall be treated with the utmost kindness,

292 compatible with the due obedience to all rules and regula-
tions prescribed to compel discipline and obedience to the
orders of the officer, or other person having them in charge.

993 This ordinance shall be in force from and after its passage, ;
approval and publication, and all erdinaneces in conflict with
this ordinance are hereby repealed.

Approved April 19th, 1872.

LOS ANGELES BRIDGE.

AN ORDINANCE to prevent fast riding and driving upon the
public bridge in this city, and to protect it from being in-
jured or defaced.

The Mayor and Common Council, of the city of Los Angeles

do ordain as follows:

899 SECTION 1. It shall be unlawful for any horseman, OF Fast riding or
, the driver of any wagon, carriage, buggy or other vehicle, or ae ee
of any kind of stock or cattle, to ride, lead or drive upon, unlawful.

over or across the publie bridge extending over Los Angeles

WINTER WATERS.

Preamble. Whereas, the subject of saving the Winter waters, and 365
extending irrigation is of the most vital importance to the
future of our growing city of Los Angeles, and which re-
quires the earnest attention of this body.

And, whereas, we are firmly of the opinion that by a
proper system of reservoirs for saving the Winter waters, the
creation of tomas and the fluming or building of cemented
aqueduets on the line of the established ditches now in use,
that a large body of land now almost worthless, might be
brought under a system of cultivation without decreasing the
supply of water heretofore flowing through the established
ditches of this city; therefore be it

Topographi- Resolved, That the City Engineer be instructed to furnish

eee woe this body as soon as practicable a topographic survey of the

Ptecenaee Bh lands of the city, together with the plans and specifications

economising for the purpose of economizing the waters of the river and

eosmeere of extending irrigation, and that he be allowed an assistant if
necessary in the furtherance of this object.
Passed, session July 10, 1878.
M. KREMER, City Clerk.

provided by the city, of the field notes of all surveys made,
and maps of the same, and full, true and correct accounts
and memoranda of the costs and expenses of all public works
and imprevements, and to keap posted in his office all plans
and specifications of work to be done for the inspection of all
| parties desiring to examine the same, and to do and perform
any and all other matters and things which may be required
of him by any ordinance of said city, or by any resolution or
other order of the Common Council of said city.
494 Src. 5. The City Surveyor shall receive no salary, but Fees.
shall be paid from time to time as full compensation for all
services rendered the city, such fees as may be prescribed by poo
the Common Council. Aug. 10, 1876.

shall not be so construed as to prohibit the said Surveyor
from charging and receiving the fees allowed by the Common

GRADING AND IMPROVING OF OLIVE STREET,
A RESOLUTION providing for the grading and improvement

of Olive street from Second to Third street.

Be it resolved by the Common Council of the city of Los An-
geles, as follows:

From 2d to 3d SECTION 1. That Olive street, from Second to Third 507

ae streets, shall be graded and improved in the following man-
ner, to-wit: The road-bed, including gutters on each side,
shall be sixty feet in width, and, excepting gutters, to be cut
down or filled up and covered with cement gravel to the
depth of eight inches, so that when so covered the center of
the street shall conform with the established grade, and to
have a slope from the center towards the gutters on either
side of one foot in thirty feet.

The gutters on each side of the streets shall be four feet
wide and paved with granite cebble stones eight inches long,
the center of the gutters to be nine inches and the sides to be
seven inches below the top of the sidewalk, and of a concave
shape, and to be well set in the clay and rammed.

The sidewalks on each side of the street shall be ten feet
wide, and filled in or cut down to six inches below the estab-
lished grade at the curb, with an incline towards the curb,
and then to be filled in with gravel to the depth of four inches.

The curb shall be of 3x12 inches redwood, spiked to posts
of redwood 4x4 inches, and three feet long, set in the ground
two feet and inside of the curb. Said posts to be four feet apart.
The top of the curb to be placed two inches below the grade.

The work to be completed within ninety (90) days after
the adoption of this resolution.

Src. 2. The Clerk of the Common Council shall certify
to the passage of this resolution, and shall cause the same to
be published once in English in the Los Angeles Daily Her- *
ald and ence in Spanish in Za Cronica, and thereupon it ~
shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted
by the Common Council at its session of April 1, 1875.

wards the gutter. They shall then be surfaced with four
inches of cement gravel. There shall be a stake of redwood
3x4 inches and two feet long, set in the greund opposite
to, and four feet inside of, each post to which the curb is
spiked. There shall also be an anchor of redwood 1x4 and
four feet long, nailed to and connecting the stake with the
posts, four inches below the top of the post.

The top of the curb shall in cases be set two inches be-
low the established grade.

The work to commence at the lower end of Temple street,
and to be prosecuted only upon one block at a time.

A RESOLUTION of the Common Council of the city of Los
Angeles providing for the construction of a public sewer,
‘to be known as Main street sewer.
Be it resolved by the Common Council of the city of Los An-
geles as follows:

519 SECTION 1. That there be and hereby is ordered to be To be con-
laid out and constructed at the expensé of the property hold- powawar oe
ers, the real estate of whom is assessable therefor, a publia &™tyY owners.
sewer in said city, to be Known and designated as Main street
sewer, along and over the following described route, to-wit:

Commencing at the intersection of Main and Arcadia pescription of
streets, running thence along Main street southerly to its in- 7°U%?
tersection with Ogier Lane, easterly to a point where it would
intersect the line of the Main sewer crossing said street.

The said sewer shall be constructed in accordance with Construction.
the following specifications: The sewer shall be egg-shaped;
the greatest interior height will be three feet, and the great- Fj
est interior width two feet, with walls eight inches thick and
built of the best quality of stock brick.

To every one thousand brick laid in the construction of
the sewer there must be two barrels of cement used, together
with a quantity of lime and sand to make a good mortar.

The inside bottom of the sewer to be a proper depth be-
low the official] grade.

No bats or parts of brick shall be used in the sewer, the
bricks to be thoroughly wet before laying.

All bricks shall be laid witha full joint of mortar, and the
bricks in the bottom and sides of the sewer for two feet in

height, to be well floated with mortar composed of equal
parts of the best cement and sand, to make it as one solid
mass.

tely made according to the dimensions of the sewer and cor-

rect form and dimensions according to the size and shape re-
quired.

on aoneeee resting on the centering until the following day, so as tobe

toinspection. examined by the Board of Public Works and the City Sur-

te injure the fresh work.

and brought up to within six inches of thé grade so as to ad-

Flanges to be A flange or connection not less than six inches in diame-

Reena ter shall be put in at and opposite each lot, and shall extend
at least one foot beyond the outer edge of the sewer andat an
angle of 45° in the direction of the descent.

Obstructions All obstructions in the way of the sewer, such as private

ea drains, gas pipes, water pipes, etc., shall be deflected from the
line so as toallow a uniform descent and line.

To be covered. After the sewer is completed in sections, the earth shall

granted. hereby granted to C. E. Beane and J. S. Crawford, and to

the purpose of laying down, maintaining and operating one
line of iron street railroad track, with two parallel rails, distant
from each other at least three feet, and to run cars thereon,

months from and after the date of the taking effect of this ordi-
nance, and shall be finally completed, equipped, stocked and

within the period of two (2) years from said date; it being un-

A RESOLUTION
To abate nuisances in the city of Los Angeles.
Be it resolved by the Council of the city of Los Angeles,
as follows:

Obstructions, SECTION 1. If any person or persops shall obstruct or 676
cause to be obstructed any public street, or alley, or sidewaik
within the limits of the city, either by riding or driving upon
the said sidewalks; or permitting their horses to stand upon
the same; or leaving carts or vehicles of any description upon
the same; or permitting or suffering any article to remain in
or upon the same so as to render the same inconvenient or
dangerous to pass; or by making or erecting any fence, rail-
ing or other obstruction across any street or sidewalk, or any
part thereof; or maintaining any fence, railing or any ob-
struction on any street or sidewalk, or any public walk, with-
out permission of the Council being first obtained; or shall
pollute or cause to be polluted any of the canals or acque-
ducts of the city by washing in and about the same, orin
any other manner; or shall herd or pasture cattle, horses
or hogs, or any other animals, or allow them to be or re-
main near the reservoir or canal of the Los Angeles City
Water Company in such a manner as to interfere with the
purity of said water; or to herd, pasture, feed or Keep any
animal on the hillside near or by the canal or reservoir of

; said Compauy, by which any impurity created by any of
said animals herein mentioned could be carried, by rain or
otherwise, so as to mingle with or in any way or manner in-
fect the water of said Company, or shall do anything which
is injurious to the health, er indecent, er offensive to the
senses; or any act which is an obstruction to the free use of
property, so as to interfere with the cemfortable enjoyment
of life and property, such persen or persons so offend-

===== PDF 453  [printed p. 451] =====

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 45%, -*

ing shall, upon conviction before the Judge of the City Court,
be fined not less than five or more than one hundred dollars,
or imprisonment not exceeding six months, or both; and
every such nuisance may, by order of the Mayor or Council,
be abated, after reasonable notice, if the nuisance is of such
a character as to require notice to the person responsible
therefor.

Sec 2. Itis further provided, that, in the event of any Obstruction
obstruction or nuisance not being removed or abated after a 20% Temoved.
reasonable notice, and the same is removed by order of the
Mayor, or otherwise, if after demand on the person so re-
sponsible therefor, the expense of removing or abating the
same is not paid, then it shall be paid by the Treasurer of
the city of Los Angeles on a warrant drawn on the General
Fund of the city, and, such warrant having been paid, shall
be deemed a debt due from the person responsible for such
obstruction or nuisance to the city of Los Angeles, and the
same shall be collected by suit in the City Court of Los'Ange-
les for money paid, laid out and expended for the use of such
person, and a judgment rendered in said case to have the
same force and effect as judgments in Justices’ Courts.

Sec. 3. All ordinaneés and resolutions conflicting here-
with are hereby repealed.

Specifications The earth to be excavated at least 8} feet deep and suf-

shall be preserved unbroken so as toallow passage of cara,

During the night lamps shall be kept burning at each end
of the excavation; said excavation shall also be strongly
guarded to prevent accident.

room, building, arbor, booth, shed or tenement to be used or

meanor, aud shall, on vonviction, be fined not less than one
hundred or more than two hundred dollars, or imprisonment

AN ORDINANCE
To prohibit the building of bonfires in the city of Los Angeles.
The Mayor and Council of the city of Los Angeles do or-
dain as follows:

SECTION 1. All persons are hereby prohibited from burn- 714
ing brush, trees, prunings from trees or other substances int
the open air, or building bonfires after the hours of seven
o’clock P. M. or before six o’clock A. M., within the limits of
this city, without permission of the Mayor or Chief of Police.

This provision shall not apply to the building of fires for
culinary or domestic purposes.

Src. 2. Any person violating the provisions of this ordi-
nance shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall,
on conviction, be punished by fine net exceeding one hun-
dred dollars or imprisonment not exceeding thirty days, or
both.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the
passage of this ordinance and shall cause it to be published
once in English in the Los Angeles Daily Star, and once in
Spanish in some newspaper in the city of Los Angeles, and
thereupon it shall take effect and be in force.

Be it resolved by the Council of the city of Los Angeles,
as follows:

SEOTION 1. That there be and hereby is ordered to be 72()
laid out and constructed at the expense of the property own-
ers and the city of Los Angeles, as the case may be, and in
manner provided by law, a public sewer to be known and

Line of sewer. designated as the Alameda Street Branch Main Sewer, along
and over the following described route, to-wit: Commenc-
ing at the intersection of Alameda and Main streets, in the

° city of Los Angeles; thenee southerly along and near the
center of Alameda street to a point about 291 feet north from

e the north line of First street.

The earth along the above described route is to be ex-
cavated not less than four feet deep and sufficiently wide to
admit of laying the pipe sewer.

The sewer to be either cement, iron, stone, vitrified or

burnt clay pipe, provided with the necessary branches or con-

Specifications » actions at every sixty feet on each side to accommodate the
property on the alignment of the sewer and Y branches op-
posite all streets crossing the alignment of the sewer, also
brick manholes not more than 1,000 feet apart.

The pipe will be 12 inches clear diameter and to be care-
fully laid with full joints of mortar composed of equal parts
Portland cement and clear, sharp sand,

In making and fitting the joints care must be taken to
point and make smooth the mortar on the inside of each
joint before the mortar sets. In refilling the earth in, over
and around the pipe care must be taken to not disrupt the
joints or displace the pipe after the same has been joined
with mortar.

The Y branches or connections for the accommodation of

the property aligning the sewer shall be each 4 inches in di-
ameter,

be 8 inches in diameter.

All Y branches to present an angle of 45° with and in the
direction of the flow of the current.

The exterior ends of the branches are to be aecurely
closed with bricks, stones or pieces of broken pipe, when not
immediately used,

All curves in the sewer to be on a radius of not less than
25 feet. .

The manholes will be of good, hard burnt brick, laid in
full joints of mortar composed of one part Portland cement
and 2} parts clear, sharp sand, with wails 8 inches thick;

the opening in the manholes will be two feet square; the tops
of the manholes to be carried up to within six inches of the
surface of the ground and each manhole to be provided with
a cast-iron cover one inch thick,

The bottom of the excavation along the whole length of
the sewer is to conform as near as possible to the shape of the
pipe.

In conjoining or connecting with the sewer extending
from Alameda to San Pedro street, care must be taken to so
conjoin as not to injure the pipe of either sewer.

The earth taken from the excavation is to be refilled in
over the sewer in layers of about a fost thick; the layers for
the first foot above and around the sewer,is to be free from
stones and other hard substances; and all layers to be well
watered and rammed, and on completion of the work the sur-
plus materials, if any, to be removed and the street or surface
ef the ground put in as good condition as 1t was at the com-
mencement of the work. Where the sewer passes under a
street car track or railroad track, the track shall be preserved
unbroken so as to allow passage for cars. Where the sewer
passes under zanjas the flow of water in the zanjas must be
maintained if necessary. In the night time, during the con-
struction of the sewer, from sunset to sunrise, lights or lamps
shall be kept burning around the excavations; said excava-
tions shall be strongly guarded with barriers to prevent ac-
cident.

The contractor to be held liable for any accident that may
occur through the neglect of any unecessary precautions to
persons, horses, animals, vebicles or property of any kind.

The city, or its officials, being in no way liable or re-
sponsible for damages.

A RESOLUTION
Of the Mayor and Council of the city of Los Angeles pre-
scribing rules and regulations for the delivery of water
due to the city in case of fire or other great necessity.
Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the city of Los

Angeles, as follows:

SECTION 1. A sufficient supply of pure fresh water for 731
the following purposes is hereby resolved and declared to be
greatly and indispensably necessary at all times to the eity
of Los Angeles; that isto say, water in sufficient quantities
for the use of the engine houses and fires, and engines, for
watering streets, public squares and parks, for flushing sewers

===== PDF 519  [printed p. 517] =====

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 517
and for all like purposes beneficial to the public, and in aid of
the health and good government of the people of the city.

Src. 2. Itshall be the duty of the Mayor tocauseand
procure all necessary connectious to be made with the pipes
and mains of any and all corporations heretofore or hereafter
formed for the purposes of furnishing or supplying pure,
fresh water to the city of Los Angeles, or the inhabitants
thereof, and engaged in said business, in order to carry out
the provisions of this resolution; and he may, when neces-
sary, call Upon the police force to aid in making or maintain-
ing said connections with said pipesand mains.

Sec. 3. Any person who shall wilfully obstruct the
Mayor, or any other person in carrying out the provisions of
this resolution, or whoshall cut off or who shall attempt to
cut off the water necessary to any of the buildings or pur-
poses herein provided for, or cause others to do so, shal! be
deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall, on conviction, be .
punished by fine not exceeding two bundred dollars, or im-
prisonment not exceeding ninety days, or both.

Src. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify tothe pase
sage of this resolution, and shall cause the same tobe pub-
lished once in English in the Los Angeles Daily Evening Ez-
press, and once in Spanish in La Cronica, aud thereupon i
it shall take effect and be in force.

| I certify that the foregoing resolution was passed
by the Council at its session of Aug. 29th, 1878.°

Clerk.
